## Our understanding and proposed approach

Kilbride Veterinary Group has three clinics in Navan, Trim and Kells, with 11 vets and 19 support staff. The clinics receive roughly 640 inbound calls a week. Orla estimates that about 38% of after-hours calls go unanswered or reach voicemail that is not checked until morning.

About half of calls concern appointment bookings or changes. Other common calls concern repeat prescriptions and whether an animal needs emergency care. The priority is to improve after-hours cover without delaying urgent care. Anything that might be an emergency must reach the on-call vet immediately.

### Proposed approach

We propose a six-week pilot at Trim, the smallest clinic, before any rollout to Navan and Kells. The proposed assistant would answer after-hours calls, handle routine appointment requests, send reminders and route possible emergencies straight to the on-call vet’s mobile. How repeat prescription requests would be handled is to be confirmed.

VetLink 4 has no API, so the assistant cannot book directly through one. Bookings would require a daily export/import process or manual entry by staff. The preferred method, its practical limits and the process for confirming appointments are to be agreed. This is an important constraint on the booking service.

Before the pilot, we propose agreeing:

- Which calls the assistant can handle and which it must pass to staff.
- How possible emergencies will be identified and transferred immediately.
- How appointment requests and reminders will work alongside VetLink 4.
- How the pilot’s results will be assessed before deciding on a wider rollout.

### Points to confirm

The preferred launch is before the spring vaccination rush in March 2027. The detailed timetable and pilot start date are to be confirmed.

Budget has not yet been discussed. Orla will raise it with the two partners.

Client records include owners’ names, addresses and phone numbers. Where call recordings would be stored remains to be confirmed. This question needs to be resolved as part of planning the pilot.

**Subject: Hybrid working from 1 January 2027**

**Who can work partly from home**
You are eligible only if your line manager agrees that your role can be done partly remotely. Employees in their first six months (probation) must work from the office full time.

**Before you start**
You must have both:
- Written approval from your line manager.
- A completed home-office health and safety self-assessment form.

How to obtain the form is to be confirmed.

You must attend the Galway office at least two days each week. Tuesday is compulsory as the team day. Agree your second day with your line manager.

You must be available from 10:00 to 15:00, whether working at home or in the office.

**Equipment and costs**
The company provides a laptop and headset. You can claim a one-off home-office allowance of up to €300 for a desk, chair or monitor. Receipts are required. The claims process is to be confirmed.

Travel between home and the office is not reimbursed. The company does not pay home utility bills.

**Confidential information**
You must not print confidential client drawings at home.

**Changes to arrangements**
The company may review or withdraw hybrid working for any employee or team with four weeks’ written notice. Reasons may include changing business needs or a drop in performance.

## Q3 2026 board summary

Revenue fell by €16,000, or 1.0%, to €1.614 million compared with Q3 2025. Gross margin fell from 40.5% to 38.6%. Athlone was the main concern. Its revenue decline more than offset growth at the other two stores.

- **Athlone:** Revenue fell by €74,000, or 14.0%, to €456,000. Gross margin fell from 40.8% to 36.1%. The sales decline followed the opening of a national-chain competitor 2 km away in June. Heavier discounting in August to hold footfall explains most of the margin fall.
- **Mullingar:** Revenue rose by €43,000, or 7.0%, to €655,000. Gross margin fell from 41.0% to 40.2%.
- **Tullamore:** Revenue rose by €15,000, or 3.1%, to €503,000. Gross margin fell from 39.5% to 38.9%.

Margins declined at all three stores. There were no one-off items in either year.

Click-and-collect launched in May. Its revenue is included in store figures and is not reported separately. Its contribution to performance is therefore to be confirmed.

Operating profit and the proposed response to Athlone’s decline are also to be confirmed.

Subject: Yesterday’s client portal outage

We are sorry for the disruption to our client portal yesterday, 14 November.

The portal was unavailable from 08:55 until 14:55, about six hours. Browsers showed a security warning.

The portal’s security certificate expired. Automatic renewal had been failing without warning since October because an internet setting had changed. The certificate was renewed at 10:40, but some users continued to see errors until full service was restored.

Our IT provider reviewed the logs. There was no unauthorised access. The expired certificate blocked connections; it did not expose your data.

Four document uploads made between 08:50 and 08:55 did not complete. We have identified the clients concerned and will contact them individually by 17 November. They will need to upload their documents again.

No deadlines were affected. Staff completed the 14 November ROS filings for affected clients using phone and email.

We have added checks on certificate renewal. An alert now goes to two people 30 days before any certificate expires.

Feeney & Walsh Chartered Accountants

Gallagher Quinn Solicitors is a small practice with three partners, four solicitors and five support staff. Our work is mainly conveyancing, probate and family law.

We are looking for an Office Manager to run the office day to day.

### The role

You will:
- Supervise our two receptionists.
- Manage the diary system, file closing and archiving.
- Manage supplier contracts.
- Liaise with our outside IT provider.

You will need at least three years’ experience in office management or a senior administration role. Legal experience is welcome but not required.

Hours are 9:00–17:30, Monday to Friday. You will also cover reception until 19:00 every Thursday for late appointments, with time off in lieu.

Pension arrangements are to be confirmed with the partners.

Send your CV and a short cover note to **careers@gqsolicitors.example** by **5 December 2026**.

Subject: Brightwash contract – commitments and concerns

Hello,

Based on this extract, the contract commits the hotel to:

- **A 24-month initial term from 1 March 2025.** It then renews automatically for 12 months at a time. Either party must give written notice at least 90 days before the renewal date to stop renewal. The exact notice deadline and how to give notice should be confirmed.
- **Using Brightwash exclusively** for all linen hire and laundry services at the premises during the contract.
- **Paying for at least 900 kg of laundry each month**, even if you use less. The price per kg and total minimum monthly bill are to be confirmed.
- **Annual price increases** on each anniversary of the start date. These are CPI plus 3 percentage points, capped at 8% in any year.

The main concerns are paying for unused laundry, being unable to use another supplier, and missing the notice deadline and becoming committed for another year.

There are also limits on what you could recover if things go wrong. Brightwash’s total liability is capped at the charges you paid in the 12 months before a claim. It excludes liability for loss of business or profits, including losses caused by late delivery.

The extract does not give delivery commitments, remedies for service failures or rights to end the contract early. These need to be confirmed in the full agreement.

I am not a solicitor. Before signing, ask a solicitor to review the full contract, particularly the renewal and notice rules, early exit rights, exclusivity and liability limits. They can advise what these mean legally for the hotel.

Kind regards

**To:** Managing Director  
**Subject:** CRM replacement for 25 users  
**Recommendation:** Choose Option B, Larchmont CRM.

Larchmont costs more, but includes the Xero link and vendor-led data migration. It also has a customs-document template. These features make it the better fit for the needs identified.

Gerard says the Xero link is essential because accounts currently re-keys every invoice. Before committing, we should confirm that Larchmont’s built-in link covers the invoice work accounts needs.

### Annual cost

| Option | Cost for 25 users |
|---|---:|
| **A: Pipewell** | €5,400 subscription, plus about €720 for Zapier: **about €6,120 a year** |
| **B: Larchmont CRM** | **€8,700 a year**, including the built-in Xero link and vendor-led migration |

Larchmont therefore costs about **€2,580 more a year**. Pipewell’s figure excludes the cost of our time for setup and migration. That cost is to be confirmed.

### Trade-offs

Pipewell has the stronger trial result. Four of the six staff preferred its interface during the two-week trial; two preferred Larchmont. It is also cheaper and can be cancelled at any time.

However, we would need to set up Pipewell’s customs fields, taking about three days of Ciara’s time, and import the old data ourselves. Its Xero connection requires Zapier at an extra monthly cost. Support is email only during business hours.

Larchmont includes migration and offers phone and email support during business hours. Its customs-document template already exists, though any further setup needed is to be confirmed. The main drawbacks are its higher price and 12-month minimum commitment.

**Decision sought:** Approve Larchmont, subject to confirming the Xero link’s coverage, migration timetable and any further setup costs.

At Reilly Joinery in Cavan, quotes took about three working days. The owner priced every job from scratch in a spreadsheet.

We built a quoting template using their last 200 jobs, with standard units and finishes priced in. We also trained the office manager to use it. The work took six weeks and finished in September 2026.

About 70% of quotes now go out the same day.

The other 30% still need the owner. These involve unusual layouts or bespoke finishes and take about as long as before.

Owner Fintan Reilly says:

“Most quotes go out the same day now. Not every job fits the template, and that's fine - those are the ones that need me anyway.”

The template handles the standard work. The owner still prices the jobs that need his judgement.
